title: Diplomacy Table
summary: A teaching console and replay app for multi-party AI negotiation simulations, letting instructors explain the settings and replay recorded runs without a backend.

contribution.roleNote: Static, reference-only build of the Diplomacy Table pages from the DTSF monorepo.

narrative.problem: A live AI negotiation demo in front of a room depends on a server staying up, a model staying responsive and a session not expiring, and instructors also need to explain the knobs, tactics and arithmetic that decide whether a deal is even possible.
narrative.decision: Publishes complete tick-by-tick recordings of real runs that play back in the actual negotiation room with no backend, each exported from one declared perspective so a delegation's view simply omits what that seat could not see.
narrative.tradeoff: A recording cannot be steered or re-read from another seat: the View As selector is locked during replay, and running a new negotiation still needs a live DTSF backend, which is a separate private system.
narrative.limitation: Three of the console's ten tabs (Connect, Delegations, Bake-off) need a live instance, and the console itself notes where rule-based tactic detection breaks down.
narrative.caveat: Recorded negotiations are AI-generated: model delegations (gemma3:12b in the gallery) play the parties, so positions attributed to real states and officials are simulated.
